settings.title: Settings
settings.description: Configure the YOLO runtime and defaults used by each page.
tooltip.train.model: Choose the YOLO model to train. Larger models can be more accurate but need more GPU memory and training time.
tooltip.train.dataset: Choose the data.yaml file that describes the training dataset.
tooltip.train.epochs: How many times the model learns the full dataset. Too few may undertrain; too many can overfit.
tooltip.train.imgsz: Image size used for training. Larger sizes can improve small-object detection but use more GPU memory.
tooltip.train.batch: Images trained together in one step. Larger batches usually require more GPU memory.
tooltip.train.device: Select the device used for training, such as an NVIDIA GPU or CPU.
tooltip.train.workers: Background worker processes used to load training data. More can speed loading but use more CPU and memory.
tooltip.train.patience: Stop training early if results do not improve for this many epochs.
tooltip.train.project: Folder where training results are saved.
tooltip.train.name: Name for this training run, used to distinguish results.
tooltip.predict.source: Choose the image, folder, or video to analyze.
tooltip.predict.conf: Keep only predictions above this confidence. Higher values may miss objects; lower values may add false positives.
tooltip.predict.iou: Controls how strongly overlapping prediction boxes are merged or removed.
tooltip.predict.save_txt: Save predictions as YOLO-format text labels.
tooltip.predict.save_conf: Include a confidence value for each saved prediction label.
tooltip.validate.dataset: Choose the dataset used to evaluate model performance.
tooltip.validate.split: Choose which dataset split to evaluate, such as validation or test.
tooltip.validate.precision: Of predicted objects, how many are correct. Low precision usually means more false positives.
tooltip.validate.recall: Of real objects, how many the model finds. Low recall usually means more false negatives.
tooltip.validate.map50: A common overall detection metric measured at IoU 0.50; higher is generally better.
tooltip.validate.map50_95: An overall metric across stricter IoU thresholds that emphasizes accurate box placement.
tooltip.mining.conf: Predictions below this confidence are treated as low-confidence cases worth reviewing.
tooltip.mining.iou: Determines whether a prediction and Ground Truth box overlap enough to match.
tooltip.builder.base: The original YOLO dataset used as the basis for the new dataset version.
tooltip.builder.report: Error Mining report used to select useful cases for the next dataset version.
tooltip.builder.ratio: Controls how added samples are divided among train, validation, and test.
tooltip.builder.copy_base: Copy the original dataset into a new version without changing the original.
tooltip.builder.include: Add selected hard cases to the new dataset version.
tooltip.builder.overwrite: Allow replacing an existing output folder. Confirm it contains nothing you need.
tooltip.runtime.python: Python executable used by the YOLO runtime.
tooltip.runtime.yolo: Ultralytics YOLO command used by Train, Predict, Validate, and Export.
tooltip.runtime.managed: An isolated Python environment created and managed by YOLO Trainer UI; it does not modify system Python.
tooltip.runtime.cuda: Whether the current PyTorch installation can use NVIDIA GPU acceleration.

tooltip.simple.model_profile: Fast uses a smaller model; Balanced is a general starting point; High Accuracy may need more time and GPU memory.

tooltip.simple.runtime: Training requires a usable YOLO runtime. CPU-only training is allowed but may be much slower.
